parsed.headline: Man with Down syndrome killed during Israeli raid in southern Syria

pages.text: Residents and Syrian state media reported that Muath Salama Al-Baeer, a man with Down syndrome, was killed by Israeli forces during a raid on the village of Jamla in Syria’s Daraa province. According to residents, Al-Baeer was unarmed and lived with his sisters after the death of his parents. Local sources told North Press that the 30-year-old man was shot and left wounded for hours without medical assistance. Al-Baeer was buried in Jamla on a Thursday as local anger grew regarding Israeli incursions in the area. The Syrian state news agency SANA reported that a “civilian with special needs” was killed during the incursion but did not provide specific details on how the death occurred. Jamla is located outside the Israeli-occupied zone, though reports indicate Israeli forces frequently conduct incursions into areas beyond that territory. Following the ouster of former Syrian President Bashar Assad in December 2024, Israeli forces seized and have occupied a UN-patrolled buffer zone in southern Syria. While Israeli officials initially described their presence as temporary, they have since stated an intention to remain in southern Syria indefinitely to protect Israel’s borders. Syrian officials have called for an Israeli withdrawal but have not responded militarily. The Israeli military stated that during an overnight operation, soldiers identified a suspect approaching them and initiated a suspect apprehension procedure. The military said the suspect continued to approach, prompting soldiers to fire to remove the threat, and noted the incident is under review.

parsed.headline: Ghanaian President Mahama expresses intent to seek ceasefire from President Putin

pages.text: During an interview with the Financial Times at its Africa Summit on October 21, 2026, Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama stated he would attempt to persuade Russian President Vladimir Putin to agree to a ceasefire in the war in Ukraine. Mahama said he intends to make this attempt during his upcoming travel to Russia for the Russia-Africa Summit. “I’m going to Russia for the Russia-Africa Summit and try to convince President Putin to have a ceasefire if I can,” he said. The remarks were made during a discussion regarding Ghana’s relations with global powers and Russia’s involvement in security operations in the Sahel region. Regarding Russian military involvement in the Sahel, Mahama noted that Russia’s Africa Corps, which succeeded the Wagner Group, provides technical training and logistical support to some countries. He stated that countries in the region should be able to receive assistance from any partner willing to help fight terrorism, adding, “My opinion is that anybody who is committed to the fight against terrorism is welcome.”

parsed.headline: Two Syrian security members killed during anti-ISIS operation in Damascus countryside

pages.text: Two members of Syria’s Internal Security Forces were killed and five others injured on Thursday during a security operation targeting an Islamic State (ISIS) cell in Rankous, located in the western Damascus countryside, according to a statement from the security forces reported by the North Press Agency. The operation was conducted in cooperation with the General Intelligence Service. 11. According to the statement, members of the suspected ISIS cell refused to surrender and opened fire on security forces, leading to clashes that resulted in the deaths and injuries of the personnel. The security forces reported that the operation resulted in five cell members being neutralized and six others being arrested. Authorities also reported seizing weapons and explosive belts during the operation in Rankous. 12. This incident follows separate operations announced earlier this month by the Internal Security Forces and the General Intelligence Service against suspected ISIS cells in the Damascus countryside and Homs governorates. Additionally, the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA) reported that on October 16, two agencies announced the arrest of two suspects and the seizure of an explosive device during an operation intended to prevent an alleged attack on a police patrol in Rural Damascus.

parsed.headline: NDC members raise security concerns over Kwabre East constituency executive elections in Ghana

pages.text: Members and sympathizers of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Kwabre East constituency of Ghana have raised concerns regarding alleged security threats ahead of the constituency executive elections scheduled for October 17, 2026. During a press conference at Mamponteng on Thursday, Saeed Abdul Mumin, the NDC Ward Secretary for Fawoade-Bampenase, alleged that intimidation and threats are creating fear among party members prior to the internal contest. Mumin claimed that supporters of certain aspirants have received verbal warnings and threatening messages from opponents, including claims that pepper spray would be brought to the venue. These allegations have not been independently verified. The members expressed uncertainty regarding whether the polls can be conducted peacefully and credibly given the prevailing atmosphere.

The concerned members have questioned the decision by the Constituency Election Committee to hold the election at the Islamic Hall at Aboaso-Zongo, citing local information regarding security risks. Mumin argued that the hall is not an open or easily accessible public space and noted that its proximity to the residence of the incumbent constituency chairman, who is seeking re-election, could raise perceptions of bias. Additionally, Mumin accused the Kwabre East Municipal Chief Executive, Joseph Amankwah, of openly campaigning for certain candidates, alleging his conduct undermines expected neutrality. Charles Owusu, the Branch Organiser for Achiase, stated that members have petitioned Amankwah, who also chairs the Municipal Security Council, as well as the Ashanti Regional Minister and the Ashanti Regional Police Command.

parsed.headline: Deforestation in Brazil’s Amazon and Cerrado savanna reaches lowest recorded rate

pages.text: Data from Brazil’s National Institute for Space Research (INPE) indicates that deforestation in the Amazon rainforest and Cerrado savanna fell to 3,335 square kilometers (1,288 square miles) between August 2025 and July 2026. This figure represents a decrease of nearly 42% from the previous year and marks the lowest rate of deforestation recorded since satellite monitoring began in 1988. According to the report, incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva presided over these levels, which are the lowest ever recorded in both the Amazon and Cerrado regions.

parsed.headline: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney visits Turkey to establish strategic partnership

pages.text: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney arrived in Turkey on Thursday for a two-day visit, marking the first bilateral visit by a Canadian prime minister to the Mediterranean country. During the visit, Carney met with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the Turkish presidential palace in Ankara. The two leaders announced that the relationship between Canada and Turkey would be upgraded to a strategic partnership, covering trade, energy, and people-to-people ties. Both nations, which are members of the NATO military alliance, also agreed to deepen their defense relationship. Carney, a former central banker, stated that the partnership is intended to create new opportunities for businesses and workers while providing greater security and prosperity for both peoples.

President Erdogan stated that negotiations for a free trade agreement between Canada and Turkey are scheduled to begin before the end of 2026. Erdogan expressed a goal to increase current trade volume, which is approximately $3 billion (€2.6 billion), to $5 billion and eventually $10 billion, and noted plans to approximately double direct flights between the two countries. As part of the visit, Carney is expected to meet with Turkish business leaders in Istanbul on October 16, 2026.

parsed.headline: Money supply outpacing production growth fuels inflation in Bangladesh

pages.text: A World Bank report states that money supply outpacing production growth in Bangladesh is fueling inflation, as government borrowing creates a liquidity surge while private-sector credit flow slows amid production deceleration. According to the report, broad money growth, encapsulated as M2, accelerated from 6.5 per cent in June 2025 to 12.4 per cent in May 2026, while inflation remained elevated through FY2025-26. The development financier predicted that the link between broad money and inflation may be strengthening, as monetary expansion increasingly coincides with persistent price pressures. The report suggests that monetary expansion may be contributing more directly to price pressures than in previous years, when the relationship between money-supply growth and inflation was described as less pronounced. The World Bank noted that growth in M2 has been driven by increases in both net domestic assets (NDA) and net foreign assets (NFA). Previously, moderation in money-supply growth was partly driven by substantial foreign-exchange sales by Bangladesh Bank (BB), but recent developments indicate a shift in the relationship between liquidity and prices.

parsed.headline: Chiricahua rock spires in Arizona designated as newest US national park

pages.text: President Donald Trump signed legislation on Tuesday to establish Chiricahua National Park in south-eastern Arizona, making it the 64th national park in the United States. The 19-square-mile (49-square-km) site, known among Native Americans as the Land of Standing-Up Rocks, was designated a national monument in the 1920s to preserve pinnacle-shaped rocks formed by an ancient volcanic eruption. The bill passed Congress with bipartisan support. 1920s-era designation was intended to protect the hundreds of rock spires that characterize the landscape. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum stated that the area's rock spires, biodiversity, and Apache heritage make it an extraordinary landscape that will create opportunities to strengthen local economies and welcome visitors. The site is located within the historical territory of the Chiricahua Apache tribes, who resided there for centuries before surrendering to US troops in 1886 and being forcibly removed to the San Carlos Apache reservation. The legislation preserves tribal access for traditional ceremonies and allows for temporary public closures within the park to protect those cultural uses, though US Representative Juan Ciscomani of Arizona noted that specific details regarding these closures have not been decided.
